Maya Chen: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to pick a default affinity model for service API keys: per-org (default) vs per-project. Also want to nail the fallback semantics when a project-bound key hits a quota or is revoked.

Raj Patel: high-level tradeoff: per-org = simpler for infra, easier reuse across projects, but weaker isolation. per-project = stronger isolation + audit, but more noise and churn for infra.

Sam O'Neil: +1 on isolation for regulated customers. Question: how do we enforce RBAC if we allow org-scoped keys to access project resources? do we shadow-check project permissions at runtime?

Leo García: runtime check options: 1) validate token -> resolve org->allowed-projects list -> runtime ACL. 2) attach a short-lived derived project token when caller presents intent. Option 2 needs lightweight mint service and cache.

Maya Chen: Thinking about operational SLOs: option 1 is cheaper (single check) but pulls authz graph on every request unless we cache aggressively. option 2 adds latency on minting but lets us keep per-request checks minimal.

Sam O'Neil: For minting path, can we re-use existing token-broker? That'd reduce engineering lift. Also need to consider telemetry so billing maps correctly.

Raj Patel: telemetry: require the original key id to be propagated in traces/spans; accounting can aggregate by org or project depending on affinity. We should include a "source_key" field in the event schema.

Leo García: fallback semantics proposal: if project-bound key is rate-limited, try the org-backed fallback only if the org has an explicit policy that allows it (opt-in). Otherwise return 429. This prevents silent cross-project spillover.

Maya Chen: opt-in fallback + explicit allow-list on the org seems safe. We should also add an audit log entry when fallback is used.

Sam O'Neil: RBAC enforcement detail: when org-fallback is used, attach a restricted derived token that includes only the intersection of allowed project perms. That avoids accidental privilege escalation.

Raj Patel: thumbs up. We need to model TTL for derived tokens (short, e.g., 1m) and a cache keyed by (original_key_id, project_id, requested_scope).

Leo García: implementation note: cache miss path -> mint -> write audit log before returning token so we can reconstruct events if mint service fails mid-request.

Auth-Bot: deploy:auth-mint-service v0.2 rolled to staging at 2026-03-21T14:02:10Z :rocket:

Maya Chen: Next steps: draft a mini-RFC capturing: affinity default, opt-in fallback policy, derived-token flow (TTL, cache), telemetry fields, audit events. I'll write the doc and tag reviewers. Anyone want to pick ownership for the mint/proxy work?

Raj Patel: I can own the mint service PRs.

Sam O'Neil: I'll take the RBAC integration and tests.

Leo García: I'll own runtime cache + eviction policy.

Maya Chen: thanks — creating the mini-RFC now. I'll ping when it's ready for review. :thumbsup:
